title: Workday Adaptive Planning - Demo - Financial Forecasting

hook.text: In this demo, we're going to quickly and easily create a rolling forecast, and do variance analysis on the latest actuals using an automated and error-free process.
hook.technique_other: agenda statement: the narrator announces what the demo will show over a logo build and a static title card, then the product dashboard scales in

summary.tone: Calm, matter-of-fact corporate product walkthrough: a measured narrator walks an FP&A-director persona through a month-end forecast workflow in the real app, framed on a clean white-and-blue brand stage.

signature_moments.description: The dashboard slides left to reveal a 'Situation' panel whose three bullets switch from a light tint to dark ink exactly as the VO names each one (w31-w33, w37-w39, w43-w46).
signature_moments.why_premium: Word-synced highlighting turns the persona set-up into a readable, scannable brief and is the one place where on-screen text carries the story without sound.

signature_moments.description: Camera push-ins on the recording card enlarge the Name field, date picker and version dropdown so the typed 'May Forecast' and the selected rows become legible.
signature_moments.why_premium: Directing the eye with scale instead of showing a dense full-window capture is what separates an edited demo from a raw screen recording.

signature_moments.description: The same animated logo build (wordmark wipe, product-line fade, arc draw-on) opens and closes the video, the end version adding the free-trial URL.
signature_moments.why_premium: Bookending with an identical animated lockup gives the piece a finished, branded frame and a clean CTA.

hook.evidence: Opens on a logo build and a static title card while the narrator reads an agenda ('In this demo, we're going to...'); no question, pain or visual payoff in the first seconds, and the title card is misspelled ('Financial Forcasting').

clarity.evidence: Clear linear story (situation, import actuals, copy budget to a May Forecast, review P&L, compare versions) with a persona panel, an orange callout on the Apr 2021 column and push-ins on key inputs; held back by dense full-window tables that are illegible at video scale.

ui_showcase.evidence: Real product in a drop-shadowed window over a branded blue-arc stage with several targeted zooms, but long static holds (s008 ~28 s, s023 ~10 s, s030 ~11.5 s) and many loading spinners and 'Please wait...' modals are left in.

motion_polish.evidence: Motion is limited to the logo builds, a few scale/zoom reframes of the recording card and the s004 panel slide; most of the runtime is raw recording with unedited load states and sub-second flash shots (s012, s014, s022), so pacing feels unedited.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchors plus visuals: only four SFX candidates in 163 s (x001 music, x002 and x004 unsure, x003 impact-like), integrated loudness -17.83 LUFS and a ~99 BPM detected beat suggest a quiet music bed under VO; no UI clicks or whooshes line up with the many on-screen state changes.

vo_script_quality.evidence: Clear, well-paced narration with a concrete persona and month-end scenario and some benefit lines ('It's that quick and easy', 'Instead of a slow and painful copy and paste exercise'), but it is mostly feature narration of clicks and ends on a hand-off to a next demo rather than a payoff.

brand_consistency.evidence: Identical animated logo lockup bookends the video and every UI shot sits on the same white stage with the brand-blue arc and shadowed window; the misspelled title card is the main lapse.

works_muted.evidence: No captions or callout copy beyond the s002 title, the s004 Situation bullets and one orange highlight in s010; the workflow steps and benefits are carried almost entirely by the voice-over.

overall.evidence: A competent, clear corporate product demo with a consistent branded frame and a few smart zooms and word-synced highlights, but long raw-recording holds, leftover loading states, a weak agenda hook and minimal sound design keep it well short of premium.

localization_friendliness.notes: Added overlay text is small (title card, Situation bullets, end-card URL) and easy to replace, but the English product UI is baked into every screen recording and the story depends on the VO, so localising means re-recording the VO and ideally re-capturing the app in the target locale.

build_hint.gsap: Keep the window frame static. tl.set(spinner, {autoAlpha: 0}) then tl.fromTo(sheet, {autoAlpha: 0}, {autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.05, ease: 'none'}) - essentially a hard swap timed just after the narration pause.
build_hint.remotion: Render the spinner until the event frame, then switch to the sheet layer; optionally opacity: interpolate(frame, [f0, f0 + 1], [0, 1], {extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}).

events.notes: Screen-recorded page load; the change is a near-instant swap (energy peak in one frame), not an authored animation. skeleton_resolve is the closest canonical match (spinner rather than skeleton bars).
